blocking_constraints.description: Marking qualifiedDividends/ordinaryDividends as modeled in fjs/return/scope WITHOUT simultaneously wiring Form 1040 lines 3a/3b (fjs/form1040/core, which today sets them to declaredZero and hardcodes qualifiedDividendsCents: 0n) makes the engine report a confident ZERO for dividend income where it currently refuses honestly.
blocking_constraints.why_it_matters: Strictly worse than the refusal it replaces, and the exact failure TAX-16's scope guard exists to prevent.
blocking_constraints.mitigation: ROADMAP Phase 12.1 criterion 2a requires both edits in ONE atomic change. Reject at plan-check any plan touching one without the other.

Phase 12's roadmap scheduled building a QDCGT worksheet that already existed (634 lines, Phase 10) and its criterion 1 required an fjs/return/ edit the same document forbade.
blocking_constraints.mitigation: Every phase marked Research: YES must have research read the actual modules its criteria name and report contradictions as findings. Both were found before any code was written; neither would have been caught by executing the plan as written.

blocking_constraints.description: Phase 12.1 edits fjs/return/scope and fjs/form1040/core — the two modules the showcase demo anchors into most heavily. TWO separate breakages follow, and only the first is mechanical. (1) Source anchors slide: Phase 12 adding four fields to fjs/return/profile moved six demo anchors, each still returning HTTP 200 while landing in the wrong place. (2) Step 4 'Refusal' CHANGES MEANING: its whole gesture is 'declare dividend income, the entire return refuses'. Once 12.1 models dividends, that return will compute instead, and the step will silently demonstrate the opposite of what its narration claims.
blocking_constraints.mitigation: After 12.1 merges, re-run BOTH demo checks before the demo is shown again: the anchor audit (resolve every anchor at the new pin and read the line back — a path-exists check misses all of it) and a read of step 4's narration against what the engine now actually does. Procedure and rationale: demo/todo/showcase-demo.md, sections 'Re-pin' and 'Source and proof links'.

context_notes: The session's through-line, and it decided the outcome twice: THE PLANNING DOCUMENTS WERE WRONG AND ONLY READING CODE CAUGHT IT. Phase 11's CONTEXT asserted a security property the shipped code did not have; Phase 12's roadmap scheduled building something that already existed while forbidding the edit its own criterion required. Neither would have been caught by executing the plans faithfully — both would have passed their own gates and shipped something subtly false. The corollary shaped every subsequent dispatch: subagents were told to try to FALSIFY the phase's own premises, and told that finding a premise unimplementable would be the most valuable thing they could return. That instruction produced both findings. Second theme: a green mutation gate is not automatically a meaningful one. M1 reddened a real production assertion; M3 reddened a fixture assertion sitting in front of the thing it appeared to guard. Both 'passed'; only one bought coverage.
